schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: THE RULING INTAKE GATE — the door Akien's rulings come through before any code moves. He rules; the ruling becomes a schema-gated JSON packet in `CairnCommons/decisions/` carrying HIS WORDS VERBATIM beside my one-line reading, plus the two lists that make the reading checkable: `what_dies` and `what_conforms`. The intake door (`cairn.ruling.ruling.open_ruling`) refuses a malformed packet with EVERY reason at once, refuses paths that are not on disk at intake, refuses a reading longer than 280 chars or wider than one line, and refuses a packet that confirms itself — then stamps `confirmed: false` and measures a sha256 of each conformer, so neither field can be authored by the thing being gated. `verify` is the mechanical verdict: UNCONFIRMED until Akien signs off, STILL ALIVE if something ruled dead is on disk, UNTOUCHED if a conformer is byte-identical to intake, VANISHED if a conformer was deleted instead of changed. A Stop hook (`--hook`) reports every red ruling every turn and never blocks. SUPERSESSION IS THE RETIREMENT DOOR (grown 2026-08-02 against the first superseded ruling, exactly as filed edge (d) predicted): `supersede <old> <new> "<evidence>"` retires a misfiled packet by stamping the CONFIRMED successor — never the retired record, which stays on disk byte-identical, red under `verify`, and visible in `list`, but no longer OPEN, so the hook stops naming it. Refuses, with every reason at once: empty evidence, unknown ids, self-supersession, an unconfirmed successor (my guess cannot outvote his signature), a doubled retirement, and retirement by a packet that is itself retired. CLI: `cairn ruling open|list|verify|confirm|supersede`.
why: MEASURED 2026-07-31, the day this was built: four times in one session Akien's stated intent and the code's shape disagreed, and the code won. Two hours went to one of them — his ruling that `_model.json` was retired existed only as conversation, while the compiler that wrote the file existed as source with green proofs. WHEN DRIFT COMES, WRITTEN BEATS SPOKEN, and there was nothing written on his side of the room. That is not a discipline problem, it is a missing artifact: a ruling with no address is a ruling the next reader reconstructs from the code, which inverts the direction authority actually flows (code and its proofs are evidence of what was BUILT, never of what is INTENDED — a green proof means conformance to a spec, and a spec is exactly what a ruling changes). The store this writes to already existed and held exactly one entry, authored AFTER a different ruling got lost and had to be reconstructed from a transcript; this is that store's intake door, so the reconstruction stops being the normal case. Akien's own framing of the ask: 'should we just build the completely deterministic prebuild step to limit what opus tries to do?'
the_honest_line_between_physics_and_not: PHYSICS: the shape refusals, the intake-time disk checks, the measured fingerprints (from the working tree, or from git at the commit `as_of` names), verify's check that a thing ruled dead STAYED dead, and — since 2026-08-06 — its refusal to read a MISSING baseline as a passed check. None can be talked around. NOT PHYSICS: whether I heard him correctly in the first place — no deterministic step can do that, and a charter claiming otherwise would be the hollow build. What the gate buys is that a misreading surfaces as three wrong lines at minute one, red-pennable in thirty seconds, instead of as an hour of code built on top of it. The COST of being wrong drops by two orders of magnitude; the RATE of being wrong is untouched. Stating this here because the value of the thing is exactly this distinction, and a later reader who blurs it will trust the gate for something it never claimed.
invoke: `cairn ruling open <packet.json>` (refuse, or write), `cairn ruling list`, `cairn ruling verify <id>`, `cairn ruling confirm <id> "<his words>"` (Akien's act; the evidence string is required and refused empty), `cairn ruling supersede <old-id> <new-id> "<evidence>"` (retire a misfiled packet; stamps the successor, never the retired). Import: `from cairn.ruling import ruling`. Hook: `bin/cmd/ruling --hook` on Stop, wired in `.claude/settings.json`. `CAIRN_ROOTS_PARENT` overrides the two-root parent so the proof runs against a temp world. Prove: `python3 cairn/ruling/proofs/test_ruling.py` (exit 0 = green), or under the tester.
node_class: device (instrument) — CC-facing tooling in class-space; stdlib only, no runtime state of its own, fires only when invoked or when the host's Stop hook pokes it (event, not poll). Its records live in CairnCommons (knowledge — losing them loses knowledge), not beside this code.
which_prebuild_step_this_is: `I-prebuild-cognition-compiles` step 1, ORIENT — parse the request, ground it in what is ACTUALLY being asked. Deliberately NOT step 3, SURVEY, which grounds the request in the existing code and is already built as `cairn/orient/`. That intention names them as distinct steps with one module each, and names Survey as the one that gets skipped; 2026-07-31 measured the complementary failure — Orient is the one that gets OVERWRITTEN, by Survey's own output. Folding this into `cairn/orient/` would put the overwriter and the overwritten in one module.
entry: FRESH build 2026-07-31, same session as the failure that produced it. No graft. The shape borrows from two things already in this tree and cites them rather than copying: `bin/cmd/turnscan` (a Stop hook that REPORTS and never blocks, because the disposition is the owner's) and the trouble lane's rule that a live item stays in the inbox until explicitly cleared. What is NEW: the verbatim-beside-the-reading field, and the intake-time fingerprint that makes UNTOUCHED unfakeable.
state_and_history: compiled to state.json + history.json beside this charter once its ticket exists — the charter-state-history split. Built ahead of its ticket by Akien's direct instruction ('yes, do that') on a day when the workflow chain itself was the thing under repair; the ticket is a filed edge below, not a silent omission.
how_it_learns: Yes, and the corpus is its own store. Every packet is a labelled pair — Akien's words, and my reading of them — so the store accumulates exactly the training signal for the failure it exists to catch: the rulings where he red-penned the reading are the ones where the code's shape pulled me off his intent, and they are readable together, in one folder, sorted by date. The second signal is the verdict trail: a ruling that goes red long after confirmation is a ruling I obeyed and then drifted from, which is a different defect than misreading it and wants a different fix. Neither is compiled yet — today the store is small enough to read by hand, and building a learner over an n of one would be the eagerness the prebuild intention explicitly warns against ('migrate on evidence, not on eagerness').
filed_edges: (a) NO TICKET YET — built under direct instruction ahead of the workflow chain it belongs to; the ticket owes its state/history sidecars

(b) NOTHING MAKES ME OPEN A PACKET. The Stop hook reports packets that EXIST; it cannot see a ruling that was never recorded. Measured rather than assumed, before reaching for the obvious hook: ruling-shaped language fires on 28.5% of 855 real Akien prompts, so a lexical UserPromptSubmit detector is noise — and noise gets trained away while still LOOKING like coverage. The falsifier is kept re-runnable at `cairn/ruling/corpus.py` (`python3 -m cairn.ruling.cli --corpus`) so the number cannot decay into folklore. Ceiling: the host's LLM-adjudicated prompt hook, the same one turnscan names for its sibling residue.

(c) HALF RETIRED 2026-08-06. `what_conforms` verification is CHANGED-SINCE-A-BASELINE, not conforms-to-the-spec. TWO things were wrong with that and only one is still true. RETIRED: the baseline used to be the packet's own INTAKE, which silently required the paperwork to precede the work — so a ruling recorded after its own commits could never go green, and on 2026-08-05 that produced five UNTOUCHED lines on a carried-out ruling and nine live files parked under `what_dies` because it was the only field left that could. `as_of` now names the commit each root stood at when he ruled; git renders the bytes, the door fingerprints them. STANDS: changed-off-the-baseline still is not conforms-to-the-spec. The second is not mechanical, and a reader who wants the stronger claim wants a proof, not this gate.

(d) GROWN 2026-08-02, residue only. The first superseded ruling arrived on schedule: a packet misfiled /intent's SKILL.md under what_dies, so Akien opened every session to the hook telling him '/intent was ruled dead and is on disk' — which read exactly like his skill being deleted, when he had ruled no such thing. The retirement door now exists (`supersede`). GROWN AGAIN 2026-08-06: `supersedes` was a single slot, so a second retirement by the same successor silently overwrote the first — measured, not predicted, and the same-old-id guard could not see it because the overwrite landed on the NEW record. It is a list and the act appends. The case is ordinary rather than exotic: a successor must be confirmed before it can retire anything, so a packet rescoped before Akien signs the original leaves BOTH open for one correction to answer. RESIDUE: supersession retires a whole packet by a confirmed successor; there is still no door for Akien to RESCIND a confirmed ruling he has changed his mind about — today that is a new ruling plus a supersession, two acts where his mind made one move. Grows against the first real rescission.

(e) FILED 2026-08-06, the finding under the finding. NOTHING CHECKS A `what_dies` LIST AT INTAKE. The door verifies each path EXISTS — it never asks whether the corpus still depends on it. Two packets sentenced `cairn/base/probe.py`, which eight live modules import, and every mechanical check they passed was green. The lived symptom, and the reason this is an edge and not a shrug: Akien reads `now_the_spec_says`, agrees with it because it is right, types confirm — and a nine-file kill list nobody has ever looked at becomes an authoritative instruction. The physics is a grep for importers of each dying path, run at intake, refusing a packet that kills something still referenced. Same shape as /sorted refusing a drifted workflow string: one fix at the door, or whatever the execution broke. Trouble: `troubles/what-dies-sentences-files-the-corpus-still-imports`.
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_ruling.py, runnable bare (python3) and under the tester. Durability gate: not done until proven AND the VALIDATION is persisted beside-code AND committed (git).
falsifier: RED, by physics, on any of: (1) a packet without `the_ruling_verbatim` is accepted — the reading would then have nothing to be checked against, which is the pre-gate state; (2) the intake door reports one refusal where several apply (the author is made to play twenty questions — the incomplete-diagnostic defect); (3) a `what_dies` or `what_conforms` path that is not on disk at intake survives (an invented target); (4) a packet carrying `confirmed: true` is written, or the door does not stamp it false (the recorder signs its own reading off); (5) `verify` returns green while unconfirmed (confirmation becomes decorative); (6) a file ruled dead that COMES BACK does not go red — the exact 2026-07-31 regression, replayed as test_the_day_this_was_built; (7) an authored `conforms_fingerprint` survives the door, making UNTOUCHED talk-around-able; (8) the hook blocks a turn, or exits non-zero, or reports 'something is open' without naming which ruling and why; (9) a confirmation is written without the evidence of who gave it — this gate's own defect one layer up, found the first time the verb was used for real; (10) a `kind: "decision"` record in the same store is verified, migrated or overwritten; (11) `supersede` mutates the retired packet's bytes — the whole point of the door is that his confirmed act survives untouched; (12) a retired ruling still prints from the hook, or an unconfirmed/unsourced/doubled supersession is accepted, or a retired packet retires another; (13) a `what_conforms` path with no baseline fingerprint verifies GREEN — never measured is not the same as measured and green, and the weakest possible check must not wear the strongest verdict; (14) one successor retiring a second packet erases the first retirement's evidence, or a legacy single-slot `supersedes` stops retiring what it retired; (15) `as_of` fingerprints a path that did not exist at that commit — a file born after the ruling is a new build, not a conformance.
proof: proofs/test_ruling.py — seventeen teeth a hollow gate could not pass, in a synthetic two-root world (the live CairnCommons store is never read or written): every refusal on the first pass; a packet holding only my reading is refused; a padded or multi-line reading is refused; an invented target is refused in both directions; a ruling that moves nothing on disk is refused; a path cannot both die and conform; the recorder cannot self-confirm and is stamped down if it tries; the fingerprints are measured, not authored; unconfirmed is red over a perfect tree, and UNCONFIRMED is the ONLY failure there; the 2026-07-31 regression replayed (ruled dead, killed → GREEN, regenerated → RED); an untouched conformer is red; a conformer deleted instead of changed is red; a confirmation is refused without its own verbatim source and records who said so beside the flag; the older narrative decisions are neither scanned nor touched; absolute paths are refused; the hook names the ruling and its failure and exits 0 either way; and edge (b)'s corpus measurement still runs (the instrument asserted, never the moving value). NON-VACUITY is inside test_the_day_this_was_built: the confirmed-and-conforming tree must be GREEN before the regression is introduced, so the reds cannot be the gate reddening unconditionally. SUPERSESSION'S SIX TEETH (2026-08-02, replaying the misfile that grew them): every supersede refusal on the first pass; an unconfirmed successor cannot retire a confirmed act; the retirement writes ONLY to the superseding record — the retired packet is asserted byte-identical; a superseded ruling leaves the hook but stays on disk and stays red under verify; a doubled retirement and retirement-by-the-retired are refused (the two-act mutual-silencing hole); an unrelated red is not silenced; and the hook goes quiet after a CLI supersession, exercised end-to-end at the real surface.
owner: CC owns the code (cairn/ruling/ + bin/cmd/ruling) and its proof, and gates writes to them. AKIEN OWNS CONFIRMATION — the `confirmed` flag is the one field this component will not write for itself, and that is the whole point of the component (Law 6: the owner alone gates writes, and delegated confirmation is not confirmation). The records are owned by the decisions store in CairnCommons; this is its intake door, not its owner.
traces_to: Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy — 'read his intent, not the code's shape' was policy all of 2026-07-31 and lost four times)
Law 3 (nothing is known until measured — the packet turns a heard ruling into a written claim that can be falsified in thirty seconds)
Law 7 (errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces — every refusal on the first pass, and a red ruling prints every turn until cleared)
Law 6 (Akien alone gates the confirm flag; the recorder cannot self-confirm)
Law 1 (a ruling becomes structure once; the resolver stops reconstructing it from the code)
memory akien-outranks-the-code (the feedback this component is the physics for)
provenance: Born 2026-07-31 out of the session's own failure, at the end of a day Akien described as 'a disaster… it's literally taken all day to get back to zero.' He named the shape of the fix as a question — 'should we just build the completely deterministic prebuild step to limit what opus tries to do?' — and ratified the narrowed version ('yes, do that') after it was scoped down from a full prebuild pipeline to a single gate at the one seam that had failed four times that day. THE FIRST PACKET THROUGH THE DOOR IS THIS RULING ITSELF (2026-07-31-the-ruling-intake-gate), opened before any of the files it names were edited, which is both the dogfood and the first real test that the door works outside its proof. THE FIRST CONFIRMATION FOUND THE NEXT DEFECT, minutes later: Akien typed `cairn ruling confirm <id>` into the session rather than into a shell, so the act was genuinely his while the keystroke was mine — and a bare `confirmed: true` could not tell those apart. Fixed before the flag was ever written: `confirm` now requires his words verbatim and records them beside `confirmed_by`, because a confirmation with no written source is precisely the failure this component exists to prevent, wearing this component's own clothes.
